title: BTC to XMR and Bitcoin UTXOs: Coin Selection, Change Outputs, Fees, and Privacy

friendlyUrls.anchor: swap BTC to XMR without KYC

keyQuestions: What is a UTXO in a BTC to XMR swap?
Why can a BTC wallet use several inputs for one transaction?
Why can a Bitcoin transaction show two outputs?
Can many small UTXOs increase the Bitcoin network fee?
Can UTXO consolidation reveal links between BTC addresses?
Does receiving XMR hide the original Bitcoin deposit transaction?
quickSteps: Inspect the wallet preview and confirm the current BTC deposit address before signing.
Check how many UTXOs the wallet selected if the network fee looks unexpectedly high.
Treat change as a normal wallet-controlled output, but avoid unnecessary address reuse.
Avoid merging unrelated UTXOs only for convenience when preserving separation matters to you.
Verify the amount, fee, inputs, and destination one final time, then send only when the transaction matches the active route.

issueRouting.start: What should you check when your BTC to XMR deposit transaction shows unexpected inputs, outputs, or fees?

branches.if: The transaction uses several inputs and the fee looks higher than expected.
then: Check how many UTXOs the wallet selected.
Compare the transaction size and proposed feerate before signing.
Use coin control only if you understand the fee and privacy trade-offs.

branches.if: The transaction shows a second output that you do not recognize.
then: Verify the swap deposit address and amount first.
Check whether the wallet identifies the second output as change.
Do not assume two outputs mean bitcoin was sent to the wrong destination.

branches.if: You are considering consolidating UTXOs before the swap.
then: Check whether the UTXOs came from contexts you intended to keep separate.
Consider the trade-off between future fee efficiency and visible input linkage.
Avoid unnecessary consolidation when preserving separation matters.

riskNotes: Combining several ordinary Bitcoin inputs can create visible relationships between UTXOs that were previously separate.
Repeated Bitcoin address reuse can make transaction history easier to cluster and follow.
A change output is normal, but it remains part of the public Bitcoin transaction graph.
Many small UTXOs can increase transaction weight and therefore increase the total fee at the same feerate.
Receiving XMR does not erase or hide the Bitcoin transaction that funded the swap.
